name: chart-history
description: Configuration keywords for 'plot item create chart-history'. Draws a line chart of one or more recorded histories. Engine-agnostic core-kernel item shared by PFC, FLAC, 3DEC, MPoint, and MassFlow. Unlike geometry items, a chart-history has no automatic data: you must bind each trace with the 'history <name>' keyword, or the chart renders empty.
notes: The 'history <name>' argument is the history NAME (the Name column shown by 'history list'), NOT its numeric ID. A chart-history created with no 'history' keyword, or with an ID / a name that no history has, produces an empty chart (axes only, garbage auto-scale) and raises NO error. This is the most common cause of 'plot history draws nothing'.
chart-history is engine-agnostic: the same keywords apply in PFC, FLAC, 3DEC, MPoint, and MassFlow.

These keywords are not officially documented by Itasca; they were verified empirically on all five engines — PFC3D 7.0, FLAC2D 9.7, MPoint3D 9.7, 3DEC 9.0, and MassFlow 9.7 — with identical behavior, including the name-vs-id empty-chart trap, plus 'plot export datafile'. chart-history is a shared core-kernel command.
Use 'plot <name> export datafile filename <f>' to dump the exact keyword state of an existing chart built in the GUI.

chart-history plots any history the engine can record. Create the history first, name it, then bind that name. Per-engine history commands: pfc: model / ball / clump / wall / contact / measure / rblock / fish history ...; flac: model / zone / gridpoint / structure / fish history ...; 3dec: model / block / block contact / structure / fish history ...; mpoint: model / fish history ... (material-point quantities); massflow: model / fish history ... (drawpoint / flow quantities)
Empty chart with an absurd axis exponent (~1e301): no valid trace is bound — pass the exact Name from 'history list' (a numeric ID silently binds nothing).
Curve flat at zero: the model has not cycled since the history was created, so only the initial sample exists.
Enumerated live on the unified 9.x kernel (verified FLAC3D 9.7, 2026-08-13). 'begin'/'end' window the plotted step range; 'skip' subsamples points.

keywords.description: Bind a history trace to the chart by its Name. Repeat the keyword to overlay multiple traces on one chart.
keywords.name: history <name>

keywords.description: Cross-plot the bound history against another history (x = the 'vs' history) instead of the default 'vs step'. Applies to the trace it follows.
keywords.name: vs <name>

keywords.description: Show or hide the chart item without deleting it (default on when created)
keywords.name: active on | off

keywords.description: Trace draw style: line (default), or point / line-point variants
keywords.name: style

keywords.description: Per-axis scaling. 'log on|off' toggles log scale; 'minimum <v>|auto' and 'maximum <v>|auto' set fixed or automatic limits.
keywords.syntax: axis-y log on minimum auto maximum auto
keywords.name: axis-x / axis-y

keywords.description: Reverse the direction of a trace's x or y axis (default off)
keywords.name: reversed-x / reversed-y

keywords.description: Restrict the sampled range of a trace: first step, last step, and stride (0 = full range / no skip)
keywords.name: begin / end / skip

keywords.description: Show or hide the trace legend (on by default)
keywords.name: legend active on | off

examples.command:
plot create 'hist'
plot 'hist' current
plot 'hist' item create chart-history history 'ratio'
examples.description: Chart the history named 'ratio'. Confirm the name first with 'history list' (Name column, not ID). Use case: Plot a single history vs step

examples.command: plot item create chart-history history 'ke' history 'ratio' history 'unbal'
examples.description: Repeat 'history <name>' for each trace; all share the same axes. Use case: Overlay multiple histories on one chart

examples.command: plot item create chart-history history 'axial-stress' vs 'axial-strain'
examples.description: Stress-strain style x-y curve instead of vs step. Use case: Cross-plot one history against another
Render the current chart to PNG (works headless via the bridge). Use case: Export the chart to an image
